about.title: About us
about.lead: An independent research group founded in 2025, with members now based at different universities.
about.body: Nabla Lab was established on 1 March 2025 as an independent academic community, growing from a student-led group at Harbin Institute of Technology, Weihai. Its early focus was research and research training. Our members share an undergraduate educational background in the HIT (Weihai)–University of Strathclyde cooperative programme. Today, our members pursue academic paths at different institutions. Our main goal is to continue working together on research questions and shared projects. Alongside this collaborative work, we support research training and share methods and practical experience. Our interests span fluid mechanics, wave–structure interaction, marine engineering, computation, aerodynamics and the low-altitude economy.

nameOrigin.title: The name Nabla
nameOrigin.lead: Nabla Lab takes its name from ∇ (nabla), the differential operator that appears in the Navier–Stokes equations describing fluid motion.
nameOrigin.body: The name reflects our shared interest in fluid mechanics.

research.title: Our research
research.intro: Four themes connect our members’ current research interests.

themes.title: Fluid Mechanics & Computation
themes.description: Our interests include computational fluid dynamics, theoretical analysis and physics-informed neural networks for studying fluid motion.

themes.title: Waves, Structures & Marine Engineering
themes.description: Our interests include wave loading, gap resonance, fluid–structure interaction, structural mechanics and offshore renewable energy.

themes.title: Aerodynamics & Noise
themes.description: This work concerns UAV aerodynamics and noise reduction, drawing on fluid mechanics and aeroacoustics.

themes.title: Low-altitude Economy
themes.description: Our interest in low-altitude aviation focuses on engineering questions related to UAV aerodynamics and noise.

publications.title: Fluid resonance in the narrow gap between side-by-side boxes with different corner configurations
publications.summary: Using a two-dimensional viscous-flow model in OpenFOAM, the study examines fluid resonance between two fixed boxes with sharp, chamfered or rounded corners. It explores how corner shape, corner dimensions and incoming wave amplitude affect resonance and nonlinear wave responses.
publications.finding: Smoothing the corners shifts resonance towards higher frequencies and increases the resonant wave response. The study connects these changes to flow separation, viscous dissipation and higher-harmonic contributions.
